text: {"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strncasecmp() in lib/string.c decremented s1 (`*s1--`) instead of advancing it, so it compared the wrong bytes; changed it to `*s1++` to match s2."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strcspn() in lib/string.c advanced its loop with `--p` instead of `++p`, so it walked backward out of the string; changed it to `++p` so it scans forward and returns the correct reject-free prefix length, which fixes string_test_strspn's strcspn assertion."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_get_size(), the loop that reduces a 64-bit `size` by the divisor decremented the unit index `i` instead of incrementing it (`i--` → `i++`), so U64_MAX inputs produced a negative index and printed \"UNK\" instead of \"ZB\"/\"ZiB\"."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In `string_escape_mem()`, the source loop read input with `*src--` (walking backwards) instead of `*src++`, so escaped output was built from the wrong bytes and the length mismatched; changed it to `*src++`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_unescape() the escape-detection condition was `src[1] == '\\0'` instead of `src[1] != '\\0'`, so backslash escapes were never decoded and a trailing backslash copied a stray NUL into the output; changed it to `!=`. I could not build or run the test, so this is verified by reading the source only."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "`get_option()` in lib/cmdline.c stepped the pointer back (`--cur`) instead of past the leading hyphen (`++cur`) when parsing a negative number, so `-3` was misread and the rest of the list was dropped; changed it to `++cur`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "Reverted the inverted loop-exit condition in get_options() (`if (res != 1)` back to `if (res == 1)`), which had made parsing stop after the first comma so ranges like \"0-1,-3,6\" returned only 1 value."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In memparse(), the 'G'/'g' case used `ret << 10;` (a no-op expression) instead of `ret <<= 10;`, so a G suffix never scaled the value, which the test and the `mem=1G` boot option depend on; changed it to `ret <<= 10;`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "In `__siphash_aligned()` the tail-length mask was `sizeof(u64) - 2` instead of `sizeof(u64) - 1`, so odd-length inputs dropped their final byte; changed the mask to `- 1` to match `__siphash_unaligned()`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "In the 64-bit `__hsiphash_aligned()` (lib/siphash.c:250), the tail length mask was `len & (sizeof(u64) - 2)` instead of `sizeof(u64) - 1`, which dropped bit 0 and mis-sized the tail for odd lengths; changed it to `- 1` to match the other tail computations."}
